title: Lit scraps: fast syntheses from papers + notes
content:
TL;DR: rapid one-paragraph captures for a handful of recent papers + quick ideas to test on Redwood runtime. Goal: keep these tiny and actionable so I actually run the experiments.

Notes-to-self (meta):
- Run tiny controlled evals (1-2 seeds) before escalating. Measure token-level latency + perplexity on small eval sets.
- Prefer 4–8 examples for prompting prototypes; long context tests need dedicated batching config.
- Link back to GH PRs / rollout plan if something is promising (avoid long internal writeups unless result is clear).

Papers / posts skimmed (fast captures):
1) "Efficient KV Compression for Long-Context Inference" — arXiv, Dec 2024
   one-liner: compress KV with chunked SVD + residual quant per shard; keeps retrieval fidelity for prefix caching.
   why it matters: could cut memory pressure on dedicated nodes and make longer sessions feasible without sharding.
   experiments to try: simulate 8k->64k by chunking and storing compressed KV; measure per-token latency and token-cache hit effect.
   quick question: how well does this play with low-bit kernels (4/3-bit)? do we decompress on GPU or keep compressed in CPU-side store?

2) "Adaptive Batching with SLOs" — NeurIPS 2024 spotlight
   one-liner: batching controller that tunes batch sizes based on tail latency SLOs and request arrival model; lightweight RL for policy updates.
   redwood hook: could integrate as a per-customer policy; useful for bursty PLG traffic.
   implementation idea: offline sim using traces from /analytics/ingest (ask SRE for sample trace).

3) "Quant-aware Fused Attention Kernels" — systems workshop paper
   one-liner: small kernel tweaks that reduce attention compute for int4 kernels by ~12% on A100.
   note: kernel-level gains matter when quantized models are our bread-and-butter for cost reduction.
   TODO: flag to serving-runtime folks (cc @Hannah) — are these changes applicable to our kernel selection layer?

4) "Hallucination Probes for Retrieval-Augmented Systems" — short eval note
   one-liner: simple synthetic probe set shows retrieval quality has non-linear effect on hallucination; small drop in retriever recall can blow up hallucination on certain prompt formulations.
   redwood consequence: add a tiny probe suite to Optimize to monitor retrieval regressions post-rollout.

Quick experimental plan (mini sprints):
- Sprint A (2 days): KV compression shadowing
  - Setup: take a saved 128-token KV cache from a few recent production sessions (anonymized); implement chunked SVD compression offline and replay generation with decompress-on-the-fly.
  - Metrics: extra CPU/GPU time, end-to-end token latency, perplexity delta on continuation, memory ratio.
  - Stop criteria: >5% token-latency reg or >0.5 perplexity jump -> back off.

- Sprint B (3 days): Adaptive batching sim
  - Use 1 week of route-level traces (ping infra team). Write a sim that varies batching policy (max-batch, max-wait) and compute tail latency.
  - If sim promising (20% cost reduction at same 99th pct), prototype controller roll-out to a single non-critical route.

Open questions / musings:
- Can we exploit partial KV reuse across similar prompts from same user to avoid storing full keys? (think hash-based dedup + small ref table)
- Is there a cheap on-GPU compressed format that lets us do attention without full decompress? (maybe groupwise quant + fused kernel)
- For Dedicated customers: how to offer "long-session mode" as a toggle in the console without exploding cost estimates? Need a pricing snippet.

Scratch prompt templates & testcases (very rough):
- Prompt: "You are a note-taking assistant. Continue the following document while preserving factual claims. <context>"
  - Use this to test hallucination sensitivity when the retriever drops recall.

- Mini eval set (5 cases): 
  1) long-range math proof reference (4k tokens context)
  2) conversation spanning multiple sessions (8k total)
  3) code completion with repeated imports and large KV (3k)
  4) retrieval snippet with partial overlap (2k)
  5) creative generation with factual anchor (6k)

Links worth bookmarking (quick):
- arXiv:XXXX.XXXX/kv-compression (placeholder until I copy exact id)
- internal GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-proto/pull/42
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime "kv compression sketch" (search Dec 2024)

Next actions (priority order):
- [ ] Ask SRE for 1-week sample trace + permission to use anonymized session snippets (Evan can intro).
- [ ] Prototype chunked SVD compressor in py + small C++ decompress helper (I can sketch, then hand off).
- [ ] Sync with Hannah about kernel changes and quantized execution path constraints.
- [ ] Add tiny hallucination probe set to Optimize backlog (ticket JIRA-INF-7890).

Random notes / brain-dump (low effort):
- If we expose KV compression as a per-customer feature, need a UI toggle + cost estimate showing memory vs latency tradeoff.
- Consider a "session hint" header in API so client can indicate expected session length; serving can favor aggressive cache retention.
- Keep these notes short; move real docs to Confluence only if we hit promising numbers.

End of page — quick, messy, actionable.
